title: Ramadan serves as a powerful lesson in humanity and brotherhood - President
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake extended his heartfelt wishes to the Muslim community in Sri Lanka and around the world, celebrating Eid-ul-Fitr, describing it as one of the most significant occasions in the Islamic religious calendar, which is celebrated upon the sighting of the new moon following a month of fasting.

title: PM Harini calls for national unity and global peace in Eid-ul-Fitr message
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya extended her wishes to Muslim devotees in Sri Lanka and across the world, celebrating Eid-ul-Fitr festival, marking the completion of a month of devoted fasting and spiritual discipline.

title: Showers expected in parts of the island today
byline: Showers or thundershowers may occur at several places in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Northwestern and Uva provinces and in Galle, Matara, Kandy and Nuwara-Eliya districts after 1.00 p.m. today (21), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: US Issues 30-day sanctions waiver for sale of Iranian oil at sea
byline: The Trump administration on Friday issued a 30-day sanctions waiver for the purchase of Iranian oil at sea to ease energy supply pressures since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.

title: Trump considers ‘winding down’ Iran war, says others must guard Strait of Hormuz
byline: President Donald Trump said the United States is “very close” to achieving its objectives in the war against Iran and signalled a potential winding down of military operations, while urging other nations to take responsibility for securing the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Israeli military says it is striking Hezbollah targets in Beirut
byline: The Israeli military said early on Saturday it was striking Hezbollah targets in Beirut, after issuing an evacuation warning for seven neighborhoods in ⁠the southern suburbs of the Lebanese capital.

title: 76 Indonesians arrested in Negombo for illegal stay in Sri Lanka
byline: A total of 76 Indonesian nationals, who were illegally staying in Sri Lanka in violation of visa laws, have been arrested today (20) during a raid conducted at a tourist hotel in the Porutota area of Negombo.

title: Nationwide retail inspections to begin Monday ahead of festive season
byline: The Public Health Inspectors’ (PHI) Union has announced that island-wide inspections of retail outlets will commence this coming Monday (23) in preparation for the upcoming festive season.

title: Opposition Leader’s Eid-ul-Fitr message
byline: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa extended his warm wishes to Muslims in Sri Lanka and around the world, celebrating Eid-ul-Fitr festival.

title: Three arrested in separate raids over possession of fuel without permits
byline: The Sri Lanka Police has arrested three individuals in three separate incidents involving the possession, sale, and transportation of fuel without necessary permits.

title: US Special Envoy emphasises strategic role of Colombo Port in global trade
byline: The United States has underscored the strategic importance of the Port of Colombo in regional and global trade, emphasizing the need for strengthened maritime security and efficient port operations.

title: Facebook offering TikTok and YouTube creators $3,000 to post content
byline: Facebook is offering larger influencers $3,000 (£2,260) a month to post on the platform, as part of its Content Fast Track programme.

title: Iran targeted but did not hit Diego Garcia base in Indian Ocean with missiles - report
byline: Iran fired two intermediate-range ballistic missiles at Diego Garcia but did not hit the U.S.-U.K. military base in the Indian Ocean, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, ⁠citing multiple U.S. officials.

title: SriLankan Airlines cancels UL231 Dubai-bound flight for four days
byline: SriLankan Airlines has issued an operational update informing passengers of temporary flight cancellations affecting its Colombo–Dubai route.

title: Fuel not issued to bowsers at Kolonnawa Terminal despite distribution plans
byline: Fuel bowser trucks that arrived at the Kolonnawa Petroleum Storage Terminal Fuel today (21) were reportedly seen turning back after failing to receive fuel, despite earlier assurances of continued distribution by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC).

title: Fifteen arrested over links to overseas organized crime gangs
byline: A total of fifteen individuals have been arrested with sharp weapons and crystal methamphetamine (‘Ice’) for maintaining close ties with two members of organized crime gangs currently residing abroad.

title: President discusses energy crisis and economic impact with party leaders
byline: A meeting between President Anura Kumara Dissanayake and party leaders was held last afternoon (20) in Parliament.

title: Sri Lanka–Japan defence ties strengthened at high-level meeting in Tokyo
byline: The Deputy Minister of Defence, Major General Aruna Jayasekara (Retd.), held a high-level meeting with the Minister of Defense of Japan, Shinjirō Koizumi, at the Ministry of Defence in Tokyo on Wednesday (18).

title: Mother and daughter killed in head-on collision in Chavakachcheri
byline: A mother and daughter were killed in a fatal road accident in the Kanakam Puliyadi area along the Chavakachcheri - Puttur road, according to the police.

title: Nicholas Brendon, star of Buffy the Vampire Slayer, dies at 54
byline: Nicholas Brendon was best known for playing Xander Harris in the hit ‘90s TV series Buffy the Vampire Slayer. The news of his death was confirmed in a post on his verified Instagram, which was also shared with The Hollywood Reporter.

title: Refiners in India, elsewhere in Asia look to buy Iranian oil after US waives sanctions
byline: Indian refiners plan to resume buying Iranian oil while refiners elsewhere in Asia are examining such a move after Washington temporarily removed sanctions to alleviate an energy crunch caused by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, traders said on Saturday.

title: North Korean leader’s teenage daughter drives tank in latest public appearance
byline: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s teenage daughter drove an army tank with her father sitting behind her in photos from state news agency KCNA on Friday, with analysts suggesting she may be training to succeed him.

title: Sri Lanka launches data collection programme to assess fuel needs of transport sector
byline: The Government of Sri Lanka has launched a special data collection programme aimed at accurately identifying the fuel requirements of transport service providers engaged in food distribution, while strengthening sectoral planning amid the situation arising from the Middle East conflict.

title: Iran fires missiles toward US-UK base in Indian ocean, Iran’s Mehr says
byline: Iran fired two ballistic missiles at the U.S.-U.K. military base Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean, the semi-official Mehr news agency ⁠reported on Saturday.

title: Iran says Natanz nuclear facility has been targeted again
byline: Iran’s Atomic Energy Organisation (AEOI) says that the Natanz nuclear facility in central Iran has been targeted again by strikes this morning.

title: Sri Lanka records significant drop in gold prices over three days
byline: A significant decline in gold prices has been recorded in Sri Lanka’s local market over the past three days, following a sharp drop in global gold prices.

title: UNP and SJB to unite for people-centric governance - Sajith
byline: The Leader of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB), Sajith Premadasa, stated that the United National Party (UNP) and the Samagi Jana Balawegaya will unite to build a people-centric country and government.

title: Abducted woman rescued from well: Daughter found in paddy field in Batticaloa
byline: Several new details have emerged regarding the incident in which a woman was reportedly abducted and later found inside a deserted public well in the Nellikkadu area of Batticaloa.

title: Shooting incident reported near Yala National Park
byline: A shooting incident has been reported near the Heenwala wildlife outpost in Kirinda, within the boundaries of the Yala National Park.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Galle, Matara, Kalutara and Ratnapura districts.

title: Sri Lanka records over 109,000 tourist arrivals in first 18 days of March
byline: The Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) announced that a total of 109,410 tourists visited the island during the first 18 days of March.

title: Officer killed in drone attack on Iraq’s intelligence headquarters
byline: An officer has been killed after a drone struck near to Iraq’s intelligence headquarters in the capital Baghdad, its national intelligence service said.

title: Weekly fuel quotas increased from midnight today
byline: The weekly fuel quotas allocated under the QR code system of the National Fuel Pass will be increased with effect from midnight today (21).

title: LPBOA warns of up to 50% reduction in bus services over fuel shortages
byline: The President of the Lanka Private Bus Owners’ Association (LPBOA), Gemunu Wijeratne, has stated that the fuel quota for buses has yet to be properly regulated.

title: Israel’s defense minister says attacks on Iran will be ramped up, war to continue
byline: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Saturday the intensity of attacks by Israel’s army and the U.S. military will greatly increase.

title: Couple injured in train-car collision at Wadduwa
byline: A motor car has reportedly collided with a train at a railway crossing in the Wadduwa area, leaving a young couple injured, police said.

title: ‘It does not appear the US is prepared to halt its aggression’ - Iranian foreign minister
byline: Iran’s foreign minister has welcomed “any initiative that can bring this war to a complete end,” adding that this conflict has “been imposed” on the country.

title: Britain’s meningitis outbreak cases rise to 34, official says
byline: The number of meningitis cases reported in a deadly outbreak linked to a nightclub in south-east England rose from 29 to 34, including 23 confirmed cases, British health officials announced on March 21.

title: Sri Lanka looks to India-backed Trincomalee project amid energy crisis
byline: Redeveloping the World War II-era oil tank farms in Sri Lanka’s eastern Trincomalee district is the “permanent solution” to the energy crisis, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said, adding that the government was taking steps to expedite the project backed by India and United Arab Emirates.

title: Fuel prices increased
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (Ceypetco) has announced a revision of fuel prices, effective from midnight today (21).
